member.summary: Provides and convenience overloads for .

remarks.para: These members historically lived in this namespace, which is different from the Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Apps.ManagerStore.Select namespace that declares . As a result they were not discovered automatically when only the Select namespace was imported.

They have been superseded by , which lives in the same namespace as . The methods below are kept (as plain static methods that forward to the new extension methods) purely for backwards compatibility: existing source that imported this namespace keeps compiling, and previously compiled assemblies keep binding to these static methods. New code should rely on instead.

member.name: P:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Messages.Advanced.SetDataMinerInfoMessage.ElementID
member.summary:
Element Location Transparency: use this property in combination with DataMinerID to send a message.
Scenarios: - both DataMinerID and ElementID filled out: message is about an element and will be sent to the correct hosting agent for that element. If no hosting agent could be mapped, it is sent to the given dmaid. - only DataMinerID is filled out, and DataMinerID is an ID of a cluster agent: message will be sent to that agent - only DataMinerID is filled out, and DataMinerID is not an ID of a cluster agent: message will be sent to the local agent - none of DataMinerID or ElementID is filled out: message will be handled by the local agent

member.name: F:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Messages.AlarmEventMessageExposers.PropertiesDict
member.summary: Properties exposed as string to string dictionary. Dictionary Key = Property Name, Dictionary Value = Property Value Creating this dictionary can lead to exceptions as the name of the properties are not unique. Two properties can have the same name but being from another type (alarm, element, service or view). To fix this we take the first property and if the same name of a property occurs again we skip it. This wil fix DCP221868. With DCP224136 we will add the types as well, so this properties can be used as a condition for hyperlinks.

member.name: T:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Messages.ElementReceiveEventMessage
member.summary: Represents an "element receive" event. Implementing a derived class must also add a new case in the following method GetSLDataMinerSubscribeElementType (DataMiner.cs)

remarks.para: Element receive events are generated in 3 scenarios

item.description: Each second, a receive event of the type is generated. This event contains the number of received data packets from the element. This value can be zero.
When a bad response is received, an event of the type is generated. These events can occur multiple times within the same second.
When a timeout was encountered, an event of the type is generated. These events can occur multiple times within the same second.

member.summary: Most severe of all rows of tables which defined in the bubble up path which have a FK to the row impacting this view. In other words: Worst(impactingRows.BubbleUpAlarmLevel)

member.name: P:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Messages.ViewStateEventMessage.DirectSystemObjectLevel
member.summary:
Alarm level of the "system object", without objects below it. The system object is the view (aggregation rules in it, not elements below it), enhancing element and all rows linked to the view via viewImpact.
Combination of DirectViewImpactsLevel, DirectEnhancedRawlevel and DirectExtraLevel

member.name: P:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Messages.ViewStateEventMessage.SubSystemObjectLevel
member.summary:
Alarm level of the items below this "system object". The system object is the view, enhancing element and all rows linked to the view via viewImpact. The objects below it are the items in the view and subviews, aggregation rules of the subview, enhancing elements of subviews and the bubble up alarm level of the linked rows.
Combination of DirectViewImpactsBubbleupLevel, SubLevel, SubEnhancedRawLevel and DirectRawLevel

member.name: P:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Messages.ViewStateEventMessage.SystemObjectLevel
member.summary:
Alarm level of the "system object", including objects below. The system object is the view, enhancing view and all rows linked to the view via viewImpact.
Combination of DirectSystemObjectLevel and SubSystemObjectLevel

member.name: M:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Messages.ParameterInfo.RemoveTableColumnPostfix(System.String)
member.summary:
If the parameter is a table column, this removes the table postfix of the description/name. There are two possibilities: - A shared postfix is present in all non-empty column descriptions. Then ColumnDescriptionsHaveTablePostfix on the table parameter will be true and _columnDescriptionTablePostfixLength of this parameter will contain the length of the postfix. - This column description has a postfix exactly matching the table description
returns null when the postfix can not be validated (because ParentTable is not known yet).

member.name: P:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Messages.ParameterInfo.RangeLow
member.summary: Lower limit of parameter range (+strings: min chars). when no range is specified.

member.name: P:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Messages.ParameterInfo.RangeHigh
member.summary: Upper limit of parameter range (+ buttons/pagebuttons: width + strings: max chars). when no range is specified.

remarks.p: Note: for parameters of type or , this field contains the width of the button:

item.description: : use max width available (width="max" in XML)
0: no width specified
-1: auto width (size of text + 10px, with a minimum of 60px)
any other value: width in pixels

remarks.p: Note2: For string parameters, this field indicates the maximum number of characters in the string.

member.name: P:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Messages.ParameterInfo.RangeStep

member.name: T:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Messages.GetAlarmDetailsMessage
member.summary:
Returns a set of objects for the given alarm trees. There are cases where you will not get results back. Here's how it works: Case 1: Alarm id given is a root alarm id AND is available in cache Flow: 1. Cache is checked for the root alarm id, a match is found and returned. Case 2: Alarm id given is NOT a root alarm id and is available in cache Flow: 1. Cache is checked for the root alarm id, no match is found 2. Cache is checked for normal alarm ids, match is found and returned. Case 3: Alarm id given is a root alarm id and is NOT available in cache Flow: 1. Cache is checked for the root alarm id, no match is found 2. Cache is checked for normal alarm ids, no match is found (given id is a root alarm id) 3. Database is queried for the root alarm id, match is found and returned. Case 4: Alarm id given is NOT a root alarm id and is NOT available in cache Flow: 1. Cache is checked for the root alarm id, no match is found 2. Cache is checked for normal alarm ids, no match is found 3. Database is queried for the root alarm id, no match is found (given id is not a root alarm id) 4. No result is returned.
Whenever a result is returned, the most recently squashed alarm is returned. For example, if you request alarm id 4117, it is possible to receive a different . It might for example have id 4220. When you check the property of that alarm however, it should contain "4117". In order to retrieve the exact alarm 4417, a different message has to be used. .

remarks.p: Messages of this type are used when composing objects.

With the RequestFullTree option enabled and data not coming from database, the result will be trimmed to respect the MaxAlarmsPerParameter setting, which means that for big trees, only the X most recent events will be returned.

member.name: M:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Messages.ResourceManagerHelper.SetReservationInstancesBulk(Skyline.DataMiner.Net.ResourceManager.Objects.ReservationInstance[],System.Boolean@)
member.summary:
Add the reservationInstances in bulk. (Editing/deleting is not supported) This method is faster than the non-bulk method, but there are some restrictions to the reservationInstances data:
All the reservationInstances must follow up on eachother, meaning that the end time of one reservation must be the start time of the next reservation.
All the reservationInstances must use exactly the same amount and kind of resources.
The reservationInstances may not have children reservationInstances.
All reservationInstances must have the same serviceDefinition (or all lack of a serviceDefinition).
All reservationInstances must have the same ReservationStatus.
All reservationInstances must have an empty ID.
If atleast one of the reservationInstance violates these restrictions, none of the reservationInstances will be added.
member.param: The reservationinstances to add
Whether or not the adding in bulked worked or not.
member.returns: The reservationInstances that were added, null if things went wrong

member.name: T:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Apps.SpectrumManager.Legacy.ISpectrumLegacyMessage
member.summary: Empty interface implemented by all legacy spectrum requests to re-route their handling to the legacy Spectrum message handler.

members.member:
Set the playback speed of the spectrum recording. This controls how quickly events are sent to the client, so the maximum speed is limited by how fast frames can be processed.
Examples: Speed = 2: Playback at double speed Speed = 1: Playback at normal speed Speed = 0.5: Playback at half speed Speed = 0: Pause until the speed is changed again Speed = -1: Rewind at normal speed Speed = -2: Rewind at double speed True if the operation succeeded, false otherwise

member.name: M:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.MigrationManager.SrmCassandraToElasticHelper.GetPropertiesConverter
member.summary: Will retrieve all the different custom properties of the objects that will be migrated to elastic in the whole cluster. These properties are then put in a converter which will apply the default properties conversion, which is: 1. Remove any conflicting characters from the property keys 2. If this causes conflicts, apply a (1), (2) suffix to the property key These conversions should be customized by the user and then used when starting the actual migration. This is a heavy call since it will read the full Cassandra database. Because of this it the call should be polled. The first time you call it, the getting of the properties is started and a SrmCassandraPropertiesAreBeingCollected error is returned. Consequence calls will also return the SrmCassandraPropertiesAreBeingCollected error until the properties are collected, then it will return the PropertiesToElasticConverter. The SrmCassandraPropertiesAreBeingCollected error also contains some extra info about the current state of the property collection.
member.exception: if the retrieving of the properties failed, containing errors. Nothing was forwarded to the cluster.
if after syncing the request to the cluster, one DMA in the cluster couldn't process it correctly and ended with an error
member.returns: all the properties of the cluster, mapped to the default conversion destination name

member.name: T:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Automation.AutomationEntryPoint
member.summary: This summary is for server developers: How to add an additional entrypoint: 1. Add a delegate in SLManagedAutomation -> AutomationEntryPointDelegates.h with the method definition you want to use as entrypoint. 2. Add an entry to the enum in SLManagedAutomation -> AutomationEntryPointType.h (AutomationEntryPointType::Types enum) 3. Construct a static readonly AutomationEntryPointType in SLManagedAutomation -> AutomationEntryPointType.h (see private: section) 4. Add the same enumvalue as you did in step 2 to the AutomationEntryPoint.Types enum in SLNetTypes. (Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Automation.AutomationEntryPoint.Types) 5. Build SLManagedAutomation & SLNet and you're good to go
member.remarks: This documentation is also present in SLManagedAutomation->AutomationEntryPointDelegates.h

member.summary: Creates a new instance.
member.remarks:
A key looks like this:
[amount of elements] [amount of DMA keys] [dma key 1] [dma key 2] ... [dma key n] [element 1 dma id] [element 1 element id] [element 1 level] [element 1 read-only state] [element 1 editable state] [element 2 dma id] [element 2 element id] [element 2 level] [element 2 read-only state] [element 2 editable state] ... [element n dma id] [element n element id] [element n level] [element n read-only state] [element n editable state] [amount of fields for view ids] view 1 view 2 view 3 [amount of fields for non-editable views] view id 1 view id 2 [amount fields for view level count] view id 1 view level 1 view id 2 view level 2 [amount of element parameters] [amount of parameters for element] dma id 1 element id 1 parameter id 1 parameter level 1 parameter read-only state 1 parameter editable state 1 parameter id 2 parameter level 2 parameter read-only state 2 parameter editable state 2 ... [amount of parameters for element] dma id 2 element id 2 parameter id 1 parameter level 1 parameter read-only state 1 parameter editable state 1 parameter id 2 parameter level 2 parameter read-only state 2 parameter editable state 2 ... ... [amount of owned key components] key exception 1 key exception 2 ... [amount of owned id components] id exception 1 id exception 2 ... [DataMinerUserId object for which the security key is meant ] ... [list of OwnershipContracts related to this user ] ... [amount of readonly views] view id 1 view id 2 ...
member.param: Key containing all permissions granted to the client using this ClientSecurity object. This key can be obtained by sending a of type

member.name: E:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Connection.OnAbnormalClose
member.summary: Called when the connection is being closed or destroyed abnormally.

remarks.p: The

example.p: Examples of abnormally closed connections include:

item.description: The server is shutting down
The client has too many messages waiting to be handled, possibly indicating hanging code in the client application.
The callback connection has become invalid. This could happen if messages got lost between server and client.
The connection was idle for too long. This means that the client did not send or receive any messages for a long period of time and the validity of a callback connection could not be checked
When the callback connection became invalid.
The connectionchecking by the client indicated that the connection is no longer valid

example.p: Note that when the server closes a connection, it is not always able to send the reason back to the client (e.g. if the callback has become invalid).

member.name: E:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Connection.OnEventsDropped
member.summary: Fired when the server (DataMiner Agent) decided to drop part of the events that were supposed to be sent over this connection. Occurs when the number of events that the server has queued for this client exceeds the limit.

item.description: The event will be fired max. 1 time.

After has been fired, new messages may still enter via . The event only indicates that the server queue has reached its maximum size at least once, and that messages have been dropped as a consequence.
A client should take appropriate actions when this event is fired. It should either notify the user that the displayed data is incomplete, or mark the connection as invalid and close it.

member.name: P:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Connection.StackOverflowSize
member.summary: The maximum size of the stack with unhandled messages. When the stack exceeds this size, the connection will be automatically closed.

remarks.p: A messages stack overflow occurs when a client application blocks while handling the incoming messages. If the connection was to be left open in this case, the application would start using more and more memory.

Note that the stack contains incoming message calls, not actual incoming messages. If messages are sent from SLNet to the client each 500ms, a StackOverflowSize of 100 would mean that the client blocked for at least 50 seconds.
A StackOverflowSize of -1 indicates that there is no overflow.

member.summary: Aborts .

member.name: M:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Filters.AlarmFilter.BuildInline(System.String,System.String,Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Filters.IAlarmFilterLoader)
member.summary:
Composes an inline filter.
Filter definition syntax:
Multiple filter items or operators separated by a hash sign # ('#')
Operators:
"and", "or", "not", "(", ")" (see AlarmFilterItemOperator.Parse)
Filter items:
field name[comparison type]value1|value2
field name => see AlarmFilterItem.ToFieldType comparison type (enclosed in square brackets) => see AlarmFilterItem.ToCompareType values => separated by pipes ('|'). Ampersands in values need to be encoded as & Pipes ('|') in values need to be encoded as &separator; Hashes ('#') in values need to be encoded as &hash;
Full definition:
e.g. "root alarm id[equal to]12|34|65#and#hosting dma id[equal to]7"
Throws an exception on invalid filters

member.name: T:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Expressions.FunctionParser
member.summary:
This class can parse the following types of expressions:
- Single value:
"value"
String values can be enclosed in double quotes (e.g. "string with a \" in it" = --string with a " in it--)
- Single function execution:
"Function(arg1,arg2,arg3,...)"
args are single values or function calls
- Comparison (yielding true/false)
expression1 operand expression2
operand is <, >, <=, >=, !=, == expression is a function call or a value == and != operators cause string comparison (case insensitive) other operators cause Double comparison
To use, call FunctionParser.ParseExpression and specify a callback to evaluate function values
Sample full expressions:
max(property("alarm.impactedclients")) > 127

member.summary: Should not occur

member.name: F:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Correlation.RuleBucketMode.SingleEventDispatch
member.summary: A bucket which is used for single events and does not evaluate conditions. Instead, each incoming alarm event is pushed into a temporary TrackCollection bucket, which will check the conditions and execute an action or register a sliding window occurrence. Sliding Window Occurrences end up in a dedicated sliding window manager bucket.

member.name: F:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Correlation.RuleBucketMode.TrackCollection
member.summary: Generated by a SingleEventDispatch mode bucket to deal with condition evaluation and action tracking of a single event. Also used to track actions on a FixedTimeWindow type of rule.

member.name: F:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Correlation.RuleBucketMode.GroupMonitor
member.summary: The bucket constantly keeps track of active alarm events, evaluating conditions whenever something changes. When conditions are fullfilled, actions are executed or sliding window events get registered (on a separate dedicated sliding window manager bucket).

member.name: F:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Correlation.RuleBucketMode.SlidingWindowManager
member.summary: Bucket responsible for gathering sliding window occurrences

member.name: P:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Serialization.ClassInfo.ObjectId
member.summary:
If the ObjectId is referenced by a MemberReference record elsewhere in the serialization stream, the ObjectId MUST be positive.
If the ObjectId is not referenced by any MemberReference in the serialization stream, then the ObjectId SHOULD be positive, but MAY be negative.
member.remarks: Windows uses a single counter that counts from 1 to generate the ObjectId in the ClassInfo, ArrayInfo, BinaryObjectString, and BinaryArray records, and the LibraryId in the BinaryLibrary record. The maximum value is 2,147,483,647. If the object is of a Remoting Type that cannot be referenced in Windows, the negative of the counter value is used.

member.summary: Describes the shape's type and can be circle, poly or rect. By default, no shape is defined.

member.name: P:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.Maps.MapMarkerImage.Shape
member.summary: The format of this attribute depends on the value of the type and follows the w3 AREA coords specification found at http://www.w3.org/TR/REC-html40/struct/objects.html#adef-coords. The coords attribute is an array of integers that specify the pixel position of the shape relative to the top-left corner of the target image. The coordinates depend on the value of ShapeType as follows: - circle: coords is [x1,y1,r] where x1,y2 are the coordinates of the center of the circle, and r is the radius of the circle. - poly: coords is [x1,y1,x2,y2...xn,yn] where each x,y pair contains the coordinates of one vertex of the polygon. - rect: coords is [x1,y1,x2,y2] where x1,y1 are the coordinates of the upper-left corner of the rectangle and x2,y2 are the coordinates of the lower-right coordinates of the rectangle.

member.name: T:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.NodeRecovery.NodeState
member.summary: Possible states of a node in the cluster.

summary.para: For local view: Initial state for nodes before an initial heartbeat has been received from that node. This occurs during startup of the NodeRecovery DxM or after remote nodes have notified that they expect to have downtime (e.g., on restarts).

For global view: A node gets marked as Unknown globally in scenarios where it is not possible to determine whether its state should be marked as Healthy or in Outage. Refer to Node Recovery for detailed information.
For local view: The node is considered to be alive from the observing node's perspective. Heartbeats have been received from this node recently.
For global view: In general, a node is marked as Healthy as soon as one voting node sees it as Healthy. See NodeRecovery docs for detailed information.
For local view: When no heartbeats have been received for a period of time from the observing node's perspective, the node is considered to be in outage.

For global view: In general, a node gets marked as being in Outage state when no voting node sees it as Healthy and a cluster majority of voters agrees that the node is in outage. See NodeRecovery docs for detailed information.

member.summary:
Objects must implement this interface if they wish to be PieceMealComparable. In most cases, the IEnumerable<PieceMeal> PieceMealCompare(T other) method can simply be redirected to: return PieceMealComparableHelper.PieceMealCompare(this, other);
The CompareTo method from IComparable and IComparable must also be implemented so the objects can be sorted.

member.name: T:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.ResourceManager.Helpers.PieceMeal
member.summary: Storage class used for PieceMealComparison This stores the differences between the objects compared.

member.name: T:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.ResourceManager.Helpers.PieceMealComparableHelper
member.summary:
Static class containing default implementation for IPieceMealComparable<T> and some helper methods
Description of PieceMealCompare: For two objects, allows to find out which of the selected (by use of PieceMealCompareAttribute) fields/properties have changed. If a field/property is PieceMealComparable itself, further detects changes at the lower level. The result of the compare can be used to make a decision on which actions to execute.

If the task execution time is larger than the interval, the next task execution will start as soon as possible after the end of the previous execution (depending on the resolution of the timer, which is 1 second by default). After this, the regular interval will be resumed. Thus: the task will execute max. one time within each interval.

: limits messages to one particular DataMiner Agent
: limits messages to one particular element
: limits messages to one particular parameter of a given parameter

member.name: T:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.TrackedSubscriptionUpdate
member.summary:
Returned for the TrackXXXX subscription methods of the Connection object. Using this object, it is simple to queue actions to be executed when the subscription update reaches certain states. Eventually, caller should call Execute() on the object to launch the actual subscription.
e.g. connection.TrackAddSubscription(...) .OnEndUpdating(() => { some actions }) .OnAfterInitialEvents(() => { more actions }) .Execute();

Output: The paging cookie that can be used in the NextPagingRequest method to request the next page. If output is 0, no cookie could be created
Output: The total amount of tickets this request would result if done as a regular request (GetTickets). If output is -1, no total amount could be calculated.
The page number you wish to get
Links to be used when searching the tickets
Filter to use when searching the tickets
Indicates whether to only check the cache (true) or also the DB (false)
member.returns: A collection of tickets of size (pagesize) matching the links and filter
member.remarks: Usage of the pageNumber is not recommended. It is much more efficient for the server to call NewPagingRequest->NextPagingRequest->NextPagingRequest->Next... Than it is to call NewPagingRequest with another pageNumber every time.

member.name: T:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.ToolSpace.DirectoryCleaner
member.summary:
This class can be used to cleanout a folder given a set of rules
- create a DirectoryCleaner object indicating the folder and max size - specify a number of rules to apply - execute the Run method
Rules are executed in order
Each rule allows to specify:
- FileNamePattern: a regex for the file name - DaysToKeep: creation time boundary. Any file older than this time will be deleted (default: unlimited) - MinEntriesToKeep: can be used to always have the latest x files available, even if these cause the size limit or DaysToKeep to be exceeded (default: 0)
The class does not work recursively. It only cleans up files directly within the given folder.
After a cleanup round, it is possible that the maximum size is still exceeded, due to other files in the folder or MinEntriesToKeep rules

member.name: T:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.ProtocolFormatStringParser
F:Skyline.DataMiner.Net.ProtocolFormatStringParser._formatItemsRegex
member.summary:
Matches format items in protocol formatting string Group[0]: The format item including the curly braces, ex: {pid:10} Group[1]: The contents of the format item, ex: pid:10 Group[2]: The type of the format item, ex: pid Group[3]: The ID or other specifier of the format item, ex: 10
The format item needs to contain text and can optionally be followed by a ':' and random text (even '}' is allowed, as long as it's escaped) Escaped curly braces are NOT matched, ex: \{pid:10} is not matched. Numbers only are NOT matched, ex: {0} is not matched Unmatched curly braces outside a format item are escaped internally, ex. {text}} is equal to {text}\} Recursive format items are supported. The parser will only match the inner format items. Run the parser again on the result to match the outer format items. For example: {cardVar:{pid:1005}} will match {pid:1005}.
Example: {sessionVar:something\}text} Will have one match with: Group[0]: {sessionVar:something\}text} Group[1]: sessionVar:something\}text Group[2]: sessionVar Group[3]: something\}text
Example 2: {0} Will have no matches.
Example 3: {elementname} Will have one match with: Group[0]: {elementname} Group[1]: elementname Group[2]: elementname Group[3]: ""
Usage: Parse the input string. Loop over the format items and build a list of values. Use GetOutputString(valueList) to generate the resulting string.

member.summary: Original string, but with unmatched curly braces escaped

The purpose of this connection is to verify that only an authenticated connection can interact with the DataGateway process. In first instance, only the SLNet process will be allowed, but once we have this authentication improved, we can e.g. allow test projects to connect to DataGateway directly.
